summary.headline: Finolex Cables Q1 FY27 revenue rose 44% to INR 2,013 crore and PAT 59% to INR 221 crore, helped by a temporary communication-cable margin spike near 30%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew about 44% YoY to INR 2,013 crore, with PBT of INR 277 crore (up about 62%) and PAT of INR 221 crore (up about 59%). PBT margin expanded to 13.4% from 11.8% and PAT margin to 10.7% from 9.6%. Electrical cables drove growth on volume and price, while communication cables margins were lifted by low-cost opening fiber inventory that management said will normalise. Copper rod revenue collapsed to INR 8 crore as the rod plant shut on LPG shortage.

segments.name: Electrical cables
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,767 crore, up about 47%. Automotive, battery, flexible, solar and agricultural cables grew high double digits in volume; building wire grew low single digits in volume as channel destocked. Management said domestic electrical margin of about 10.5% should be sustainable.

segments.name: Communication cables
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 176 crore, up about 62% from INR 109 crore, with margin close to 30%. Volumes up about 30%; INR 30-40 crore of the revenue was exports to the US and Europe. Management expects margins to normalise to low double digits by year-end as opening inventory is consumed.

segments.name: Copper rod
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 8 crore vs INR 403 crore a year ago; rod plant shut for the quarter due to continued restriction on LPG availability.

segments.name: FMEG
segments.commentary: Described as a weak link: fans were short of commercial LPG and conduit pipes short of PVC. Target of INR 5 billion FMEG revenue by FY28 reiterated, though the season was largely lost.

guidance_outlook: Communication cable margin expected to normalise; management still sees double-digit margins, likely low double digits, at year-end if demand holds.
Fiber draw capacity to rise from 4 million km to 8 million km by September 2026 (end of Q2), directly rather than in two phases.
Cabling capacity to rise from 8 million to 10 million km, with a longer timeline than the draw expansion.
Preform (100 metric ton) plant expected to stabilise in the next couple of months; management expects it to be fully functional from the September quarter. Phase 2 preform doubling under review.
FY27 capex unchanged at about INR 300 crore.
FMEG target of INR 5 billion by FY28 still intact per management.
capex_capacity: Fiber draw capacity: moving from 4 to 8 million km in one phase, completion by September 2026; original plan was 4 to 6 then 6 to 8.
Preform plant of 100 metric tons, equivalent to about 4 million km of fiber; the balance of 8 million km requires bought-in preform. Phase 2 expansion will be decided later.
Cabling capacity: one plant full, the other about three-quarters utilised; expansion to 10 million km.
FY27 capex about INR 300 crore, unchanged.
Management confirmed R&D and capex steps for data-centre-grade cables, with no details given.
demand_pricing: Fiber prices (G.652.D): about USD 5-6/km in December 2025, peaked at USD 17-18, now settling at USD 11-13/km; premium fiber sold up to USD 50/km.
Communication cable demand is driven by data-centre and AI build-outs; long-term contracts are over half of communication revenue and were repriced in late June 2026.
Electrical cables: about 60% construction, with automotive cables above 14% of the mix in Q1; LV and HV cables about 7-8% of the mix.
Electrical cable price hike of about 3% taken in May 2026 amid copper at about INR 14,000 per kg level; channel inventory was lower at quarter end.
Domestic fiber consumption about 25 million km per year vs China at 400 million km plus; management sees 50-60 million km potential.
Germanium tetrachloride supply is restricted with long lead times; supply covers the calendar year, with no multi-year contracts available.
BharatNet: no update; winners waiting given high prices.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are EBITDA margins, and how much of the expansion is one-off versus mix or copper pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Export gains came from optic fiber opportunities that may not recur, so management is conservative on them. Domestic electrical margin of about 10.5% should be sustainable; communication margins will fall as old raw material is used up, to low double digits by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What fiber prices are prevailing and how do they compare with December 2025?
qa_highlights.answer: G.652.D went from USD 5-6/km in December 2025 to USD 17-18, and is now settling at USD 11-13/km. Management declined to forecast further movement.

qa_highlights.question: How much of communication cable revenue is exports and to which geographies?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 35-40 crore of the communication revenue was exports, mainly to the US and Europe.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 100 MT preform plant lift margins by about 100 bps once it is fully functional?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not see margins improving from here and called 100 bps stretching it, given that elevated prices may not last.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue reach about INR 300 crore per quarter from fiber?
qa_highlights.answer: At USD 11/km on 8 million km a year, fiber-only sales would be about USD 88 million, or about INR 250-260 crore; cabling adds 20-30% value on top, so INR 300 crore is achievable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FMEG outlook and does the INR 5 billion FY28 target still hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed LPG shortages for fans and PVC shortages for conduit pipes; the target of INR 5 billion by FY28 remains.

risks_watch: Communication cable margin of about 30% is temporary; normalisation to low double digits as low-cost inventory runs out.
Fiber supply is tight: preform and germanium are restricted, with preform sourcing still partly external and contracts about a year long.
Input cost volatility from LPG, helium, PVC and fuel after Middle East disruption; supply chain risk to the copper rod plant.
Export revenue depends on episodic opportunities; management cannot give a repeatable export mix.
Preform contract repricing could raise raw material costs once older contracts reset.
FMEG remains weak; catching up on the lost fan and pipe season is uncertain.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes and demand, with an explicit caution that the communication margin is temporary. Management was evasive on data-centre contracts, R&D specifics and export mix, and declined to predict fiber prices.
